title: Proposal for Lifts that Can Accommodate Baby Prams, Wheelchairs and Personal Mobility Aids in Some Public Buildings
what_it_is: Proposal for Lifts that Can Accommodate Baby Prams, Wheelchairs and Personal Mobility Aids in Some Public Buildings

sections.label: Mandating lifts for prams wheelchairs
sections.summary: Asked whether Government will mandate malls and public buildings to set aside lifts for prams, wheelchairs and personal mobility aids; BCA encourages going beyond code standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Government will consider mandating shopping malls and other public buildings to plan for and set aside lift cars that are purpose-built to accommodate more users of baby prams, wheelchairs and personal mobility aids to make these places more friendly for families.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These lifts are required to have sufficient manoeuvring space for wheelchairs and accessible features, such as conveniently placed lift buttons, mirrors and grab bars that would benefit other lift users including those using personal mobility aids and prams.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: BCA encourages building owners and developers to tailor their accessible facilities to the profile of their users and go beyond baseline code standards, where needed, especially for places with high public footfall.

sections.label: Accessible lift code requirements review
sections.summary: 2019 Code requires at least one accessible lift of 1,200mm by 1,400mm with 900mm opening and side control panel; review underway, draft consultation by year end.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The current Code which is in effect would be the latest 2019 version.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It provides that where lifts are provided in a building, at least one accessible lift must be provided and it must serve all levels intended for access by persons with disabilities, has a minimum size of lift of 1,200 millimetres by 1,400 millimetres in depth, minimum lift opening of 900 millimetres and a control panel at a suitable height.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The lift car of a wheelchair-accessible passenger lift must also have a side control panel to facilitate ease of access and use by wheelchair users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, as I mentioned earlier, the current Code requirements would be large enough to benefit those using personal mobility aids (PMAs) and prams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There are PMAs and there are PMAs, and we have seen some very large PMAs that are actually more like small cars rather than what you would expect of a personal mobility device.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As the Code is currently under review, what we will do is to take this feedback on board and, if others have suggestions or thoughts on lifts, lift access, convenience of use of lifts, please do provide this feedback to BCA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As I said, the review of the Code is underway and a draft of the revised Code is targeted to be released for public consultation by the end of this year.
